newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's inflationary expectations soften - survey.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's inflationary expectations soften - survey.

text.p: Sweden's business sector has continued to lower its inflationary expectations compared to three months ago, a survey commissioned by the central bank, the Riksbank, showed on Wednesday.
The survey by economic research institute Prospera AB showed annualised inflation in one year's time is seen at 1.4 percent, in two years at 1.6 percent and in five years at 2.0 percent.
This compared to a similar survey in September when inflation in one year was seen at 1.7 percent, in two years at 1.9 percent and in five years at 2.2 percent.

The survey carried out four times a year is one of the central bank's key analytical tools used in its policy planning and is considered one of the weightiest in Sweden when it comes to forecasting inflation.
The poll involves a sample group of money market players, purchasing managers and representatives of employees' and employers' organisations.
The money market expectations were 1.5 percent in one year (compared to 1.8 percent at the time of the last poll), 1.8 percent in two years (2.0) and 2.1 percent in five years (2.3).
The Riksbank is due to present its next inflation report on December 17.
